One new ammonia plant using 3 SMR technology operated by Gulf Coast America is planned for Texas City, Texas, and is projected to produce 1.3 MM tonnes/year of NH , which is larger than most operating U.S. 3 ammonia plants (Business Facilities, 2020). The design flow rate for the SMR cases, Case 1 and Case 2, was selected to match the single-train maximum capacity for a steam methane reformer, which is approximately 200 MMscfd hydrogen (Lewis, et al., 2022). This suggests a capacity of approximately 820,000 tonne/year NH , which is larger than 84 percent of the 3 currently operating plants but less than the newly proposed Gulf Coast America plant. In contrast to the SMR technology, the ATR technology is generally regarded as scalable without the need for additional reactor trains. Two major technology suppliers for ammonia ATR 21 COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION technology include Topsoe, with their SynCOR technology, and Uhde (Kelling, 2023) (Dill, 2022). Both ammonia ATR technologies can produce approximately 1.3 MM tonnes/year NH , which is 3 selected as the capacity basis for Case 3.
